_note_tmaze4: 11-27 racing T-maze v4 (v3 kept as plan_world_korea26scan_tmaze.json; docs/.../out/analysis/tmaze_v4_2026-11-27.md): the map's only FAST blind spot -- track 16.8 m, just past the right-hand bulge of the S-bend (approach 7.5-8.5 m/s for 10 m, 6.0 m/s at the spot, corridor 2.02 m); R = 2 real boxes (0.36 x 0.30 m) from the right wall, 0.15 m gap, over the line (the line runs 0.68 m off that wall): the car must move 0.41 m left into a 0.96 m lane; any part first seen 5.3 m / ~0.6 s before (tmaze_measure, passes 2+); L = the mirror from the left wall (the line passes it, 0.96 m lane on the right), the two exclusive (common passage 0.13 m); P = (0.4, 0.4, 0.2) per episode, never removed, 32 s episodes, no opponents, --scene-replay 0. NUDGE TEST (tools/tmaze_nudge.py, scan31b2 u600, 384 envs): reacting to R costs only +0.18 s per pass (no hits), so anticipation can gain at most ~0.18 s per R pass (~0.07 s per lap) -- BELOW the 0.5 s target; a pre-sight shift costs +0.16 s on unblocked passes, an approach capped at 4.5 m/s +0.9-1.0 s. tools/tmaze_room.py: on korea26_scan every blind spot (row first seen <= 0.8 s) has no room on the free side before the sight point, and every spot with that room is seen >= 1.24 s ahead -- the occluding wall is the one that narrows the corridor. Not meant for training until a fixed occluder / divider design is agreed (see the analysis).
